title: Graph Isometry and Radical Quotient
body_html:
Graph Isometry and Radical Quotient

The map \[ (X,X')\mapsto -wX+X'w \] from source and target Lie algebra layers to \(W\) is an isometry for the symplectic forms defined by \(\Gamma\) and \(\Gamma'\). The graph of \(d\alpha\) has radical given by the deepest centralizer layer, and after quotienting by this radical one obtains a nondegenerate finite symplectic space \(b_0\). In Case II the graph is already maximal isotropic and \(b_0=0\).
proof_html: This aggregates the trace-form isometry supercuspidal_theta.lie_layer_to_oscillator_isometry, the radical computation supercuspidal_theta.radical_of_gamma_symplectic_layer, and the graph radical quotient supercuspidal_theta.graph_radical_quotient. These nodes respectively give the isometry, compute the radicals using the good-element commutator, and apply exactness plus dimension counting to identify \(b_C\), its orthogonal complement, and \(b_0\).
